skills.name: Find wavelength and wave speed; use v = fλ

note.text:
A displacement-distance graph (a wave profile) is a snapshot of the whole wave at one instant: distance runs across.
Wavelength λ is the distance between two successive points in step, for example crest to crest, in metres.
Wave speed v is how fast the wave travels, in m/s.
In one period the wave moves one wavelength, so v = λ/T, that is v = fλ.
Rearranged: f = v/λ and λ = v/f.
In a ripple tank a vibrating bar makes straight wavefronts and a dipper makes circular ones. A wavefront joins points in step, and the distance between two neighbouring wavefronts is one wavelength.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to read a wavelength from a wave profile and use v = fλ to find speed, frequency or wavelength.
Builds on: Lesson {9} (period, frequency and amplitude).
Leads to: Lesson {11} (what happens when waves meet an obstacle) and Lesson {14} (the speed of sound).

sections.heading: Wavelength and wave profile
sections.text:
A displacement-time graph follows one particle. A displacement-distance graph, or wave profile, is a photograph of the whole wave at one instant, with distance running across.
Wavelength λ is the distance between two successive points that are in step: crest to crest, or trough to trough. It is measured in metres.
In a ripple tank, a vibrating bar makes straight wavefronts and a vibrating dipper makes circular ones. A wavefront joins points that are in step, such as the tops of the ripples, and neighbouring wavefronts are one wavelength apart.

sections.heading: The wave equation
sections.text:
In one period T the wave moves forward exactly one wavelength λ.
speed = distance ÷ time = λ ÷ T, and since f = {1} ÷ T:
v = fλ.
Rearranged: f = v ÷ λ and λ = v ÷ f.
Examples:
• f = {50} Hz, λ = {0.4} m: v = {50} × {0.4} = {20} m/s.
• Sound at {340} m/s with f = {170} Hz: λ = {340} ÷ {170} = {2} m.
Keep the units together: metres with hertz give metres per second.

key_words.meaning: the distance between two successive points in step, such as crest to crest
how fast the wave travels, in m/s
a line joining points of a wave that are in step
a shallow tank of water used to show wave behaviour

mistake.why: Speed is the frequency MULTIPLIED by the wavelength: one wavelength for every vibration each second.

worked_example.problem: A wave has a frequency of {f} Hz and a wavelength of {lam} m. Find its speed.

cards.idea: Wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next, read off a displacement-distance graph.
example: crests {2} m apart means λ = {2} m
f = {50} Hz and λ = {0.4} m give v = {20} m/s

cards.idea: Rearranged: f = v/λ and λ = v/f.
example: v = {340} m/s and f = {170} Hz give λ = {2} m

check.prompt: A sound of frequency {f} Hz travels through {V.n} at {V.v} m/s. Find its wavelength, in metres.

misconceptions.explain: Divide the speed by the frequency.
λ = v ÷ f, not f ÷ v.

solution: v = fλ, so λ = v ÷ f.

questions.prompt: From the displacement-distance graph, what is the wavelength, in metres?

misconceptions.explain: {2 * lam} m covers TWO complete waves.
{a} cm is the amplitude, measured up the displacement axis.

solution: Wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next.
The graph shows {2} complete waves in {2 * lam} m, so λ = {answer} m.

questions.prompt: A wave of frequency {f} Hz has wavelength {lam} m. Find its speed, in m/s.

misconceptions.explain: Multiply the frequency by the wavelength.
v = fλ is a product, not a sum.

questions.prompt: A sound of frequency {f} Hz travels through {V.n} at {V.v} m/s. Find its wavelength, in metres.

misconceptions.explain: Divide the speed by the frequency.
λ = v ÷ f, not f ÷ v.

solution: v = fλ, so λ = v ÷ f.

questions.prompt: A wave travels at {v} m/s with a wavelength of {lam} m. Find its frequency, in hertz.

misconceptions.explain: Divide the speed by the wavelength.
f = v ÷ λ, not λ ÷ v.

solution: v = fλ, so f = v ÷ λ.

questions.prompt: In a ripple tank a bar vibrates {n} times in {t} s and the wavefronts are {lam} cm apart. Find the speed of the ripples, in cm/s.

misconceptions.explain: {n} is the number of vibrations in {t} s: divide by the time to get the frequency.

solution: The distance between neighbouring wavefronts is the wavelength, {lam} cm.
